raw_response:
I am a 60-year-old woman who has worked these 3 mu in Quzhou County for four decades. I completed senior high school back when not many girls in the village did, so I can read the extension pamphlets and understand what the agricultural station recommends — but I also know that recommendations are written for bigger farms with deeper pockets. My son and daughter-in-law work in a factory in Handan, and their wages cover most of our household costs. This farm feeds us first and earns a little cash second. With only 3 mu for six people, I cannot afford mistakes, but I also cannot afford to chase maximum yield with inputs I would have to borrow money to buy.

For wheat, I plant all 3 mu in mid-October with an improved semi-dwarf variety — I have used Jinmai 22 for several years and it does well here. I sow about 7.5 kg per mu. For fertilizer, the soil on my plot is moderately fertile after decades of careful management. I apply compound fertilizer as base at planting — roughly 20 kg per mu — which gives me some N, P, and K together. Then at jointing in late March, I look at the wheat color: if it is yellowish, I topdress with another 8–10 kg of urea per mu. This brings total nitrogen to about 12 kg per mu. It is slightly below the extension target of 15 kg, but I know my land, and I would rather under-apply slightly than overstretch my cash before the maize season. I irrigate three times: once before winter if the autumn is dry, once at jointing, and once at grain filling. Each pumping costs electricity, so I watch the sky and only irrigate when rain fails. I spray herbicide once in early spring; insecticide only if I see aphids.

The turnaround to maize is brutal — usually 3 to 5 days between wheat harvest and maize planting. I hire a combine for wheat harvest at about 50 yuan per mu. It saves our backs and buys us time. For summer maize, I plant a hybrid variety at about 2.5 kg per mu, right around June 12th–15th. Because the window is so tight, I do minimal tillage — just light cultivation or direct planting if the wheat stubble is not too thick. I put down compound fertilizer at planting, about 18 kg per mu. If July is dry during the big trumpet stage, I may topdress with a little urea and irrigate once. Otherwise maize is hardy and one irrigation is usually enough here. I apply herbicide at planting and watch for corn borer — if neighbors are spraying, I do too.

My yield expectation is about 420 kg per mu for wheat and 450 kg per mu for maize. The wheat becomes our flour for the year; the maize we sell to the grain station or feed to our chickens. Total cash outlay for inputs across both crops is roughly 1,800 yuan, which is what I can pay without touching the household emergency money.
